reason: The dome and lens both bend light, so combining them should help build the focusing front of the eye.
expectation: I expect a light-focusing eye front, though it may still need the iris to control how much light enters.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive cells and nerve cells also seem like a useful way to build the lining, but I want to start with focusing.

effect: The dome and lens focus light toward the back of the eye; the iris still needs to be added.
reaction: The converging rays make their combined job clear.
reason: The iris has an opening that can narrow, so adding it should help control incoming light.
expectation: I expect an eye front that both focuses light and controls how much enters.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive lining also needs building, but I want to finish the eye front first.

effect: The eye front is complete: the iris controls incoming light while the cornea and lens focus it.
reaction: The separate jobs of the ring and clear parts make sense.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should build the light-sensitive lining and outgoing nerve route.
expectation: I expect the light-sensitive cells to connect to nerve cells, making a lining that can send signals onward.

effect: The light-sensitive lining is called the retina, and its outgoing bundle is the optic nerve. Both initial goals are complete.
reaction: The picture makes the new names easier to connect to their jobs.
reason: This is the only offered combination; joining the focusing front to the retina should bring the eye parts together.
expectation: I expect a more complete eye that focuses light onto the retina, though it may still need to connect to the body and brain.

effect: The focusing front and retina now form an eye with an outgoing optic nerve.
reaction: The cutaway makes it clear how the parts fit together.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and connecting the eye to the body should bring it closer to the brain.
expectation: I expect the eye and optic nerve to connect to the body, though the leaf may still need to be added.

effect: The eyes are now attached to the body, with nerves running toward the brain; the leaf remains to be seen.
reaction: The connection to the brain makes the assembled eye feel useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and light reflected from the leaf should enter the eyes.
expectation: I expect the body to see the leaf, with light reaching the retina and signals travelling toward the brain.

effect: The completed sight pathway shows light reflected from the leaf reaching the retina, then nerve signals carrying information toward the brain.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the assembled parts finally used to see the leaf.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the leaf to the body was most worthwhile because it brought the focusing parts, retina and brain connection together in one clear pathway.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the completed eye to the body felt more like a necessary assembly step than an interesting decision: it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: The retina was introduced as a lining connected to nerve cells, with their fibres gathering into the optic nerve. The picture made both new terms understandable.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, but several steps had only one offered combination, so I was following the available path rather than figuring out compatibility.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter if it connected its parts to an everyday experience as clearly as seeing the leaf. The mostly single-option sequence was a little limiting, though.
